body.statement:
Suppose \(s=1\).  Define \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}\) by def:lipschitz-scan-invert.  There are finite constants \(C_1,C_2\), displayed in the proof and depending only on \(M,v,\alpha\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), if \(T_n=n\kappa_n^3\ge C_1\log(e/\kappa_n)\), then \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}\) is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal P_n\) and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}|
 \le C_2\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}\right\}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 L_n(\kappa_n)\asymp L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)
 \asymp\min\left\{1,\frac{n^{-1/3}}{\kappa_n}\right\}
\]
throughout this Lipschitz strong-signal region, uniformly over vanishing \(\kappa_n\).
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 L_\alpha=\log(32/\alpha),\qquad A_\alpha=2^{16}L_\alpha,
\]
\[
 B_{M,\alpha}=1+\log\!\left(\frac{16(1+2^{17}M)}{\alpha}\right),
\]
and define
\[
 C_r=8M+16A_\alpha+1+16M(A_\alpha+1)+8\sqrt{L_\alpha},
\]
\[
 c_3=2^{-24}M^{-1},\qquad c_2=2^{-22},
\]
\[
 C_F=2(3ec_3)^{-1/3}+12(2ec_2)^{-1/2},
 \qquad C_2=16C_r+4C_F,
\]
and
\[
 C_1=\max\left\{
 2^{27}MB_{M,\alpha},\;
 2^{15}M(8A_\alpha+1),\;
 8(8C_r)^3,\;
 2^{30}ML_\alpha
 \right\}. \tag{8}
\]
These constants are finite because \(M<\infty\) and \(0<\alpha<1/4\).  They are deliberately conservative.

For sufficiently large \(n\), \(m\ge n/8\).  Since \(H=\kappa_n/(2^{12}M)\),
\[
 N_H\le1+\frac{2^{17}M}{\kappa_n},\qquad
 \log(16N_H/\alpha)\le B_{M,\alpha}\log(e/\kappa_n), \tag{9}
\]
and
\[
 2^{-11}mH\kappa_n^2\ge\frac{T_n}{2^{26}M}. \tag{10}
\]
The first entry of (8), the signal condition, and lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization imply
\[
 P(\mathcal E_1^c)\le\alpha/8. \tag{11}
\]
The localization part of that lemma, with \(R_c=A_\alpha/(m\kappa_n^2)+1/n\), gives
\[
 P\bigl(\{|\widehat c-c_P|>R_c\}\cap\mathcal E_1\bigr)
 \le9e^{-L_\alpha}=\frac{9\alpha}{32}. \tag{12}
\]
Here \(R_c\ge16/n\), because \(m\le n/4\), \(\kappa_n\le1/8\), and \(A_\alpha>1\).

We next verify the deterministic fallbacks.  Let \(q=\kappa_n/b\).  Since \(b^{-3}=m\) and \(m\ge n/8\),
\[
 q^3=m\kappa_n^3\ge T_n/8. \tag{13}
\]
For \(q\ge1\), substitution into the definition of \(r_n\), together with \(1/n\le1/(4m)=b^3/4\), gives
\[
 r_n\le C_rb. \tag{14}
\]
Indeed, after division by \(b\), the four terms in \(r_n\) are bounded respectively by \(8M\), \(16A_\alpha+1\), \(16M(A_\alpha+1)\), and \(8\sqrt{L_\alpha}\).  Equations (8), (13), and (14) give \(r_n\le\kappa_n/8\).  Also
\[
 \frac{R_c}{H}=2^{12}M\left\{
 \frac{A_\alpha}{m\kappa_n^3}+\frac1{n\kappa_n}\right\}
 \le\frac{2^{12}M(8A_\alpha+1)}{T_n}\le\frac18. \tag{15}
\]
Thus both deterministic checks in def:lipschitz-scan-invert pass.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and abbreviate \(\theta=\theta_P\).  By prop:wald-late-identification and binary potential outcomes, \(|\theta|\le1\), while the definition of \(\theta_P\) gives \(y_P-\theta d_P=0\); division is legitimate because ass:local-compliance-strength gives \(d_P\ge\kappa_n>0\).  The conditional regression of \(U=Y-\theta D\), separately on the two sides of \(c_P\), is therefore \(2M\)-Lipschitz and has zero level jump.  Gluing its one-sided extensions at their common value makes it globally \(2M\)-Lipschitz.  Conditional on folds one through three, \(\widehat c\) is fixed and fold four is independent by ass:iid-sampling.  Hence, on \(|\widehat c-c_P|\le R_c\),
\[
 \left|E_P[\widehat y(\widehat c)-\theta\widehat d(\widehat c)
 \mid F_1,F_2,F_3]\right|\le2Mb. \tag{16}
\]
For treatment, equations (1)--(3) in lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization, now at bandwidth \(b\), give
\[
 \left|E_P[\widehat d(\widehat c)\mid F_1,F_2,F_3]-d_P\right|
 \le Mb+\frac{2\kappa_nR_c}{b}+2MR_c. \tag{17}
\]
All divisions are valid because \(b>0\).  Moreover, \(16\kappa_nR_c/b\le r_n\le\kappa_n/8\) gives \(R_c/b\le1/128\), so the displaced cutoff lies inside the kernel window.

The fold-four summands are bounded and are nonzero only when \(|X-\widehat c|\le b\), an event of probability at most \(2b\) by ass:uniform-running-variable.  Since \(|U|\le2\), their conditional second moments are at most \(8\lVert K_0\rVert_\infty^2/b\) for \(U\) and \(2\lVert K_0\rVert_\infty^2/b\) for \(D\).  Applying the moment-generating-function calculation (5), conditionally on the first three folds, yields simultaneously
\[
 \left|\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{U}(\widehat c)
 -E_P[\widehat\Delta_{4,b}^{U}(\widehat c)\mid F_1,F_2,F_3]\right|
 \le8\lVert K_0\rVert_\infty\sqrt{\frac{L_\alpha}{mb}}, \tag{18}
\]
and the analogous treatment inequality with constant four, except on an event of probability at most \(\alpha/8\).  The Bernstein linear terms are absorbed by the displayed square-root terms for all sufficiently large \(n\), since \(mb=m^{2/3}\to\infty\).  Equations (16)--(18) and the definition of \(r_n\) imply
\[
 |\widehat y(\widehat c)-\theta_P\widehat d(\widehat c)|\le2r_n. \tag{19}
\]
If \(\widehat d(\widehat c)<\kappa_n/2\), the rule returns \(\Theta\), which contains \(\theta_P\); otherwise (19) puts \(\theta_P\) in the accepted set.  Equations (11), (12), and (18) bound the total failure probability by
\[
 \frac\alpha8+\frac{9\alpha}{32}+\frac\alpha8
 =\frac{17\alpha}{32}<\alpha.
\]
The bound is independent of \(P\), proving uniform honesty.

For expected length, whenever \(\widehat d(\widehat c)\ge\kappa_n/2\), the accepted labels form an interval of length at most
\[
 \frac{4r_n}{\widehat d(\widehat c)}\le\frac{8r_n}{\kappa_n}. \tag{20}
\]
On \(|\widehat c-c_P|\le b/8\), equation (17) with \(R_c\) replaced by \(b/8\), the bound \(Mb\le r_n/8\le\kappa_n/64\), and a fold-four treatment fluctuation at most \(\kappa_n/8\) imply \(\widehat d(\widehat c)>\kappa_n/2\).  Let \(\mathcal F_n\) be the event that the rule invokes its full-length scan or denominator fallback.  This event is contained in a coarse-scan failure, a localization error larger than \(b/8\), or a fold-four treatment deviation larger than \(\kappa_n/8\).  Equations (5), (9)--(13), and lem:rectangular-jump-scan-localization give
\[
 P(\mathcal F_n)
 \le2e^{-c_3q^3}+12e^{-c_2q^2}. \tag{21}
\]
The numerical slack in \(c_3=2^{-24}M^{-1}\) absorbs \(N_H\) under the first signal inequality in (8); the localization exponent at \(b/8\) is at least \(2^{-19}q^2\), and the treatment Bernstein exponent is at least \(2^{-22}q^2\), which proves (21).  The elementary one-variable optimizations
\[
 \sup_{q\ge1}qe^{-c_3q^3}\le(3ec_3)^{-1/3},
 \qquad
 \sup_{q\ge1}qe^{-c_2q^2}\le(2ec_2)^{-1/2}
\]
turn (21) into
\[
 P(\mathcal F_n)
 \le C_F\frac{b}{\kappa_n}. \tag{22}
\]
Since \(m\ge n/8\), \(b\le2\rho_n\) at \(s=1\).  Taking expectations in (20), using the maximal interval length two on the fallback, and applying (14) and (22), gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_P|I_n^{\mathrm{SI},1}|
 \le\frac{8C_rb}{\kappa_n}+\frac{2C_Fb}{\kappa_n}
 \le C_2\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}. \tag{23}
\]
Equations (8) and (13) imply \(\rho_n/\kappa_n<1\) in the asserted region, so (23) equals the claimed minimum order.

Finally, every unknown-cutoff rule induces a known-cutoff rule that ignores the supplied cutoff.  Therefore \(L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)\le L_n(\kappa_n)\).  Combining this decision-theoretic inclusion, thm:known-cutoff-benchmark, and (23) yields
\[
 c_0\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}
 \le L_n^{\mathrm{known}}(\kappa_n)
 \le L_n(\kappa_n)
 \le C_2\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}.
\]
This proves the theorem.
body.justification: The theorem gives the paper's proved strong-signal interval frontier on the Lipschitz face through one explicit sample map.
body.gap: It closes the vanishing-jump unknown-cutoff oracle-reduction gap at \(s=1\), which neither known-cutoff weak-IV inversion nor fixed-jump cutoff estimation resolves.
body.consumer: Researchers with Lipschitz reduced forms can implement the stated four folds and use \(n\kappa_n^3\gtrsim\log(e/\kappa_n)\) as the oracle-attainment diagnostic.
